concerns.text: The plan cites 'MaxEnt-style (via scikit-learn)' as a primary algorithm. Standard scikit-learn does not natively implement MaxEnt (Maximum Entropy) modeling; it provides Random Forest, SVM, and Logistic Regression. While 'MaxEnt-style' could imply a custom implementation using logistic regression with regularization, the plan does not specify the library (e.g., `maxent` package, `dismo`, or a custom implementation) or the mathematical equivalence being used. Relying on `scikit-learn` alone for a 'MaxEnt-style' model without explicit implementation details risks the pipeline failing to produce the intended algorithm, rendering the comparative analysis invalid.

The plan states 'Data Streaming: pygbif and rasterio handle data streaming/chunking to fit memory' for climate rasters. WorldClim v2 and CMIP6 rasters are typically large (global coverage, 30s resolution). While `rasterio` can read chunks, the plan does not specify how the pipeline handles the memory load of extracting climate values for potentially millions of occurrence points across 19 variables simultaneously. Without a defined strategy for batch processing or in-memory chunking of the extraction step (e.,g., processing by spatial block or species subset), the 7 GB RAM constraint on the free-tier runner may be exceeded during the feature extraction phase, causing the pipeline to crash.

The plan asserts 'WorldClim/CMIP6: Verified to contain temperature (bio1-bio11) and precipitation variables.' While true, the plan does not cite the specific resolution or projection (e.,g., WGS84 vs. specific projection) of the rasters. GBIF coordinates are in WGS84. If the downloaded rasters are in a different projection or resolution, the extraction step will fail or produce incorrect values. The plan should explicitly state that the downloaded rasters will be reprojected/resampled to match the occurrence coordinates before extraction.
